blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: At 02:00:00 a scheduler thread sets the plain field `maintenanceMode = true`. From 02:00:05 on, request threads poll that field in a tight loop, with no lock and no volatile access anywhere in the loop. What is guaranteed about those reads?

options.text: They may return false at first, then true, since a write is ordered before reads that start long enough after it
options.says: happens-before is not time: a write made earlier by the clock gives no edge, and the page's plain flag stayed unseen for two seconds

options.text: They may return false at first, then true, since a thread's end orders its writes before all later reads
options.says: a thread's end orders its writes only before a join on it, or an isAlive() that sees it ended; the polling threads do neither

options.text: They may return false indefinitely, since nothing orders a plain write in one thread before a plain read in another
options.says: without a happens-before edge every read is allowed to return the old value, forever, however long ago the write was made

options.text: They may return false indefinitely, since nothing orders a plain write made without a lock before a plain read made without one
options.says: plain writes made without any lock do reach plain reads in other threads once an edge orders them, as the loader's map reaches the main thread through a volatile edge and a join; what is missing here is any edge, not a lock

origin.section: Happens-Before Is Not Time: a Write Seconds Earlier Can Stay Invisible

questions.stem: Thread A fills a plain `List<String> routes` and then writes the volatile field `version = 7`. Thread B loops until it reads `version == 7`, writes the plain field `routeCount = routes.size()`, and exits. Thread C calls `b.join()` and then reads `routes`; C never reads `version` and never joins A. Is C guaranteed to see the filled list?

options.text: Yes, since the volatile edge from A to B and the join edge from B to C chain into one ordering
options.says: happens-before is transitive: A's list writes come before its volatile write, B's read sees it, and B's actions come before C's join returns

options.text: Yes, since the join edge from B to C also waits for A, whose list B used
options.says: join() waits for the joined thread only; what covers C is the chain of edges, not waiting for A

options.text: No, since the volatile edge from A to B and the join edge from B to C don't chain into one ordering
options.says: happens-before is transitive, so the two edges do chain; the page's three-thread chain has the same shape

options.text: No, since the join edge carries only B's own writes and the volatile edge carries only A's flag
options.says: an edge carries every write made before its first end: the volatile edge carries A's list writes, and the join passes them on

origin.section: Four Pairs of Actions Connect Two Threads, and Transitivity Chains Them

questions.stem: The main thread runs `region = "eu-west"; batchSize = 500; worker.start(); dryRun = true;`, where all three are plain fields. The worker reads the three fields first thing. Which of the three values is the worker guaranteed to see?

options.text: All three, since the main thread's writes that follow start() are also ordered before every action of the worker
options.says: the start edge covers the writes made before the call to start(), not the ones after it

options.text: All three, since a new thread takes far longer to get going than one field write takes
options.says: happens-before is not time; a write that usually lands first is still unordered

options.text: Only region and batchSize at first, then dryRun too once the write has left the main thread's store buffer
options.says: no edge ever covers a write made after start(), so dryRun is never guaranteed, however long the worker waits

options.text: Only region and batchSize, since the main thread's writes that follow start() are not ordered before the worker's reads
options.says: a call to start() happens-before every action in the started thread, which covers the writes before the call; dryRun, written after it, is a data race

origin.section: Four Pairs of Actions Connect Two Threads, and Transitivity Chains Them

questions.stem: A producer writes the plain field `lastPrice` and then the volatile field `quoteSeq`. A consumer runs `double px = lastPrice; if (quoteSeq == expected) publish(px);`. What can `publish` be handed?

options.text: Only the expected quote's price, since the producer's two stores reach the consumer in program order
options.says: the writer's order is only half of the rule; the consumer's read of the price comes before its volatile read, so the edge doesn't reach it

options.text: Only the expected quote's price, since the volatile check covers both of the consumer's two loads
options.says: an edge carries writes only to code after its other end; the price was read before the check

options.text: An older quote's price, but only when the processor performs the consumer's two loads in the opposite order
options.says: no reordering is needed: the page's stale payloads come from the reader's own code reading the value before the check

options.text: An older quote's price, since both fields can change between the consumer's two loads
options.says: the producer can write both fields between the consumer's reads; the check then sees the new number and passes on the price read earlier

origin.section: Spot the Problem: Reading the Payload Before the Flag

concepts: A write made earlier by the clock is not ordered before a read, and may stay invisible; waiting, sleeping or timestamps create no edge.
A reader gets the carried writes only in code after its volatile read, lock or join; a plain read made before the volatile read can return a stale value.
